clue.text: Problem with boots initially is hard for cobblers

definitions.note: British slang for nonsense; the clue's noun stands for the answer as a mass noun

parts.note: a rub is a snag or difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word boots

parts.note: first letter of boots

explanation.surface: A shoe repairer complains that hard boots cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoe menders beside 'boots', but in British slang it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Get better religious education with fellow rector, at first

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of rector

parts.note: first letter of rector

explanation.surface: A rector advises taking religious education with a friend to recuperate.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health after illness.

clue.text: Dotty neckerchiefs daughter's taken off

indicators.note: taken off means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: bandanas are large patterned neckerchiefs
D for daughter; the apostrophe-s reads as 'has'

explanation.surface: Spotted scarves that a daughter has removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like polka-dot scarves, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is informal for going mad, so it means crazy.

clue.text: I had mainly simple thoughts

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: easy means simple

explanation.surface: Someone admits to having mostly simple thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions or concepts formed in the mind.

clue.text: Worker is holding tops of containers and picnic hampers

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker

indicators.note: holding means the word is wrapped around those letters
tops of takes the first letter of each word that follows

parts.note: first letters of containers, and, picnic

explanation.surface: A worker holding the lids of containers and picnic baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hampers' looks like picnic baskets, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to impede, and so are handicaps.

clue.text: Start admitting dog's tied up

indicators.note: admitting means the first word lets the second in, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a seed is the start from which something grows
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: At the beginning a dog is let in and then tethered.
explanation.definitionFit: Secured means fastened firmly, which is what tied up describes.

clue.text: Enthusiast's taken up golf getting injured

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, and the apostrophe-s reads as 'is', giving nut's
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A keen player has taken up golf and got hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stung means hurt, as by a wasp or by words.

clue.text: Many left enthralled by noblewoman

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the following word

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman, the wife of an earl or count

explanation.surface: Many are left spellbound by a titled lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too numerous to count, i.e. very many.

clue.text: Regret adolescent announced habitual procedure

indicators.note: announced means the words are spoken, giving the sound of another word

parts.note: to rue is to regret and a teen is an adolescent; said together they give the sound

explanation.surface: A teenager regrets a daily habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, regular sequence of actions.

clue.text: Relish upsetting editor with answer to clue?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the abbreviation upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: a light is crossword jargon for an answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys annoying the editor with a crossword answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A light is the crossword term for a grid answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it greatly, i.e. take great pleasure in it.

clue.text: Deal with trouble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be about or relate to a subject
second meaning: to worry or disturb someone

explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean either to have as its subject matter or to cause anxiety to someone.

clue.text: University student group united with almost everyone striking

parts.note: the NUS is Britain's National Union of Students

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A university's student body joins with nearly everyone in going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action alongside a union, but it means remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking stands out, so it is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Lacquering without third of marks disappearing

indicators.note: without means the following letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: varnishing is coating with lacquer

indicators.note: third of asks for the third letter of the word marks

parts.note: the third letter of marks

explanation.surface: Applying lacquer makes the marks vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing is a synonym for going out of sight.

clue.text: Faith in God? Only some object

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run of them hidden across the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of faith, all of in and the start of God

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether faith in God is only a partial matter, or an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or item.

clue.text: Grating sounds right next to snakes

definitions.note: the answer here is a plural noun, harsh scraping noises

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: A harsh noise comes from the right, beside some snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are rough scraping noises, like a file on wood.

clue.text: Wife stops flogging last of potions for lumps and bumps

indicators.note: stops means the letter plugs a gap inside the other word

parts.note: flogging is British slang for selling

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of potions

parts.note: the final letter of potions

explanation.surface: A wife puts an end to peddling potions for minor ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: To flog something in British slang is to sell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swellings are raised areas on the body, which lumps and bumps describe.

clue.text: Enter game, breaking consensus

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of these two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Breaking into a game by general agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general accord among a group, i.e. agreement.

clue.text: Esteemed Conservative getting horribly pestered outside

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation
horribly means the letters of pestered are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A respected Tory politician is being badly hounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected means held in high regard, as is someone esteemed.

clue.text: Speaks to district attorney about clothes

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: dresses means clothes, as a verb or noun

explanation.surface: A lawyer talks to someone about their outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to talk to them directly.

clue.text: Seems new paper's carrying article

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold the article inside them
new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newspaper apparently runs a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to look or seem to be so.

clue.text: Security is turning up in warehouse

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the other

parts.note: a depot is a storage warehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Guards are appearing at the warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money given as security against loss or damage.

clue.text: Group of soldiers keeping five European squirrels away

indicators.note: keeping means the outer word holds the letters within it

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers holds five European squirrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squirrels' seems to be animals held by the soldiers, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel away is to hoard, i.e. to put aside for later.

clue.text: Guest's face covering masking sex appeal

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s is 'is', so the definition reads as the guest is

indicators.note: masking means the outer word hides the other within it

parts.note: a visor shields the face
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A visitor wears a mask that hides their allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who calls or stays, i.e. a guest.

clue.text: Spy heartlessly halts schemes

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of spy is removed

parts.note: to stem a flow is to halt it

explanation.surface: A spy coldly stops plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems are organised schemes or methods.

clue.text: Student, a bit of a looker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a schoolchild or learner
second meaning: part of the eye, the dark opening at the centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a looker' sounds like an attractive person; read literally it is part of something that looks, an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a learner at school and the aperture at the centre of the iris.

clue.text: Uses trains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: employs or exerts, as with exercising a right
second meaning: drills or works out

explanation.definitionFit: Exercising a power means employing it, and exercising a body means training it through practice.

clue.text: Army men enjoy locking up foe

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read upwards
locking means the words lock the answer inside, a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of army through men to the start of enjoy

explanation.surface: Soldiers like to imprison the opposing side.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an adversary, the opposing side.

clue.text: Groups of sailors travel slowly we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals the word as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: to cruise is to travel at an easy speed

explanation.surface: Ship's companies move at a leisurely pace, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Crews are the teams of people who work a ship.

clue.text: Want sailors in French church

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Seamen want to be in a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack, and an absence is a lack of something.

clue.text: Panto regularly seen in that place?

definitions.text: Panto regularly seen in that place?

indicators.note: seen in means the picked letters appear inside the other word

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of panto is taken, the second and fourth

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of panto

explanation.surface: Pantomime is regularly performed at such a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto, a British Christmas stage show, is staged in exactly this kind of venue, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is the venue where pantomimes are staged every winter.

clue.text: Meet Harry first, say, but not king

definitions.note: to meet a need or demand is to fulfil it

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so these letters are worried into a new order
but not means the letter for king is left out

explanation.surface: An instruction to greet Prince Harry before the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince, beside 'king', but it is the anagram signal; R is Rex, king.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy requirements is to meet them, fulfilling what is demanded.

clue.text: Fancies gentleman in river is ignoring current

indicators.note: in means the title sits inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
sir is the title of a gentleman

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for current is dropped from the word

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A man swimming in a river pays no heed to the current.
explanation.definitionFit: To desire something is to want it, which is what fancies means as a verb.
